transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-12-06 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (SE), Sara Patel (Redwood); Carlos Mendes, Amrita Rao, Julien Martin, Nora Li (NebulaGrid)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll do a quick intro — i'm maya, ae at redwood, and with me is liam our se and sara taking notes. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Carlos Mendes: good thanks, carlos here. excited to learn more, we've heard good things about redwood's serving runtime, especially around batching and kv cache stuff.
[00:22] Amrita Rao: hi, amrita — head of integrations. main goal for us is to see if there's a straight path to integrate redwood for partner deployments on nebula nodes, and how it would look for co-sell.
[00:35] Liam O'Neill: great, quick context from redwood: we offer hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments. for partners like you we typically look at two patterns — a dedicated offering that runs on your infra with private control plane, or a direct peering model where redwood control plane talks to your agents. both can work, tradeoffs on data plane, latency, and auditability.
[01:20] Julien Martin: can you clarify the private control plane vs peering? i'm thinking about our network segmentation and we prefer not to open wide access.
[01:30] Liam O'Neill: yeah so private deployment (we call it redwood private) gives you a customer-managed control plane option. the inference runtime runs in your VPC or on-prem and logs/audit stay in your environment. peering is lighter — we manage the control plane but route data over a vpn/peering; it's faster to get going but means some metadata touches our control plane.
[02:05] Nora Li: from a security perspective, we need SOC2, SSO, KMS integration, and full audit logs. also curious about encryption in transit and at rest.
[02:18] Maya Chen: understood. we commonly do sso/saml, support kms/hsm integrations, and can provide SOC2 artifacts. we'll share the security pack after the call.
[02:30] Amrita Rao: good. commercial question — do partners get a reseller discount or co-sell margin?
[02:40] Maya Chen: yes, we have a partner program. i'll send the partner playbook and typical pricing templates. for pilots we usually provide partner credits and then move to reserved capacity or customer-managed billing depending on go-to-market.
[03:05] Carlos Mendes: ok, pilot: we want to benchmark latency and throughput for 7B and 33B models, plus a reranking flow that is very bursty. we also run k8s clusters across multi-az.
[03:20] Liam O'Neill: perfect — for 7B we'll usually run fp16 or q4_0 quantization, for 33B q8_0 may be ideal — we can test several quant profiles. the runtime picks optimized kernels and we cache kvs to reduce tail latency.
[03:50] Julien Martin: any constraints on gpu types? we run A100 and some newer grip-like cards — local name is nebula-X. transcription: the name sometimes comes through wrong, but our infra is a mix.
[04:05] Liam O'Neill: we support A100, H100-ish families; we'll need exact driver and cuda versions. the runtime can adapt but kernel perf varies. we'll include a compatibility matrix.
[04:25] Sara Patel (note): action: liam sends benchmark runbook.

[08:10] Speaker 1: the team talked about fallback strategies for capacity spikes, like routing to hosted pool or smaller models — what's typical?
[08:22] Liam O'Neill: yes automatic fallback is built-in. policy-driven routing can divert traffic to model variants or hosted capacity to keep apps online; you can set cost vs latency preferences.
[08:40] Amrita Rao: and what about data residency? some enterprise customers require data never leaves the customer's vpc.
[08:49] Maya Chen: for those we recommend private deployment or dedicated on your infra, that keeps all inference data local. the peering model is a middle ground but we avoid storing persistent logs outside the customer's control unless explicitly allowed.

[15:05] Carlos Mendes: on the GTM side, we want a tight integration where nebula sells redwood as a managed inference option on our marketplace. what do partners typically need to integrate to get listed?
[15:18] Maya Chen: usually a technical integration (deployment guide), a marketplace listing page, and joint marketing assets. we can provide a quickstart repo and a terraform module for provisioning dedicated nodes.
[15:35] Amrita Rao: terraform module is great. do you have a connector for our billing metering? we need usage callbacks for revenue share.
[15:45] Maya Chen: yes usage webhooks and event streams are available; we can push metering events to your billing pipeline or provide a daily usage export.

[25:00] Julien Martin: deep technical — how do you handle kv cache across nodes and during autoscaling? our workloads have long context windows for some customers.
[25:12] Liam O'Neill: good question. we shard kv cache and maintain continuity by routing requests to the same serving pool for sessions, and we warm caches for common prefixes. autoscaling uses a fast scale-up path but scale-down keeps a warm pool to avoid cold-start latency. there are tunables for consistency vs cost.
[26:05] Julien Martin: any limitations on session length / token limits?
[26:10] Liam O'Neill: depends on model and memory; we give perf profiles per model — we'll share redwood-verified profiles for 7B/33B/70B.

[35:30] Nora Li: compliance again — we will need an attested SOC2; also logs need to show operator actions and key rotations. how does redwood surface audit logs?
[35:45] Sara Patel: we expose audit logs via the console and via an API; logs include route/model changes, deploys, and key events. for private deployments logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[36:05] Nora Li: ok, good. and what about KMS? we need a bring-your-own-key flow.
[36:12] Liam O'Neill: BYOK is supported for private and dedicated; we integrate with customer KMS or HSM. keys stay in your KMS, we store only ciphertext and use wrapped keys. we'll share the KMS integration guide.

[44:10] Amrita Rao: pilot scope — suggestion: 4-week pilot, 2 models (7B eval + 33B rerank), exclude PII, test across two AZs with 3 nebula-X nodes. success metric is p95 latency < 350ms for 7B and cost within x of our current baseline.
[44:35] Maya Chen: that sounds doable. we'll draft a pilot SOW and include benchmark scripts and telemetry dashboards.
[44:48] Carlos Mendes: timeline — if we start week of 12/15 can we have a benchmark by 12/30?
[44:56] Liam O'Neill: aggressive but feasible if we get test creds and sample workloads this week.

[52:30] Maya Chen: to recap, action items: i'll send partner playbook + pricing and a deck, liam will send benchmark runbook and request test cluster access, amrita will share topology and throughput, julien will provide node specs and access, nora will share compliance contacts. we'll schedule the se deep dive next week — propose 60 min.
[52:55] Amrita Rao: yes, please propose times. thanks everyone.
[53:05] Carlos Mendes: thanks — looking forward.
